title: Factors associated with completing group pelvic floor muscle training among referred women: a cross-sectional study linking booking records and a translated survey
abstract: Objective: to identify recorded factors and reported barriers associated with completing four or more sessions of group pelvic floor training. Design: cross-sectional study of all women referred in one year, with booking records for everyone and a translated survey linked to attendance with consent. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Group pelvic floor training works when women attend, but routine services see far lower attendance than trials, and no study has linked women's reported barriers to their recorded attendance.
methods: All 1,112 referrals between September 2025 and August 2026 were included. Recorded factors and attendance were extracted from booking records; a 20-item survey in three languages with two reminders asked about barriers, and answers were linked to records with consent. Prevalence ratios came from Poisson models with robust variance, weighted for nonresponse.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present response by attendance and language, completion by recorded factor for all referrals, and barriers by attendance for linked respondents.
discussion: The discussion will separate modifiable barriers from fixed factors, weigh nonresponse among non-attenders, and state which class changes the findings support testing.
limitations: Nonresponse, recall, inconsistent interpreter recording and one service.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will describe associations, not the effect of any change to the classes.
reportingChecklist: STROBE (cross-sectional) and CHERRIES for the online survey
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
